Hi Alice — thanks for the clear list. Pasting a concise operational summary below so your security and procurement teams have something they can map to the DPA clauses. Attaching the DPA extract (redwood-dpa-data-persistence-v1.2.pdf) and a tentative purge calendar (backup-purge-calendar.ics).

Operational timelines (proposed / default):
- Soft-delete grace period: 30 days from request. During this period data is logically deleted from application indexes but retained in encrypted object storage and snapshots for rollback.
- Hard purge of primary store: initiated at day 31, completes depending on object-store async job load (typical window: 24–72 hours).
- Snapshot retention (managed snapshots): 90 days (hot), moved to cold snapshots and purged at 180 days. Snapshots that contain customer data are flagged for purge on day 180.
- Backup replication to secondary region (for customers with cross-region replication): snapshot copies are also scheduled for purge at the same 180-day mark; deletion requests trigger cross-region tombstoning immediately and purge at the scheduled cycle.
- Logs & audit traces: default retention is 90 days for high-fidelity request logs; aggregated metrics/anonymized telemetry is retained 365 days.

Exceptions and special cases:
- Audit/Legal hold: If a legal hold or regulatory inquiry is raised, we suspend purge jobs for the affected account until the hold is lifted; we require a formal hold ticket and expected duration.
- Extended log retention (e.g., for post-incident debugging or eDiscovery): we handle via an "exception request" workflow. The customer fills the exception request doc; infra approval (karthik) + privacy signoff (kimberly) required. Typical approval SLA: 3 business days.
- Subprocessor snapshot retention: our cloud snapshot provider (listed in the subprocessor appendix) retains snapshots per the schedule above. If a customer requires snapshot deletion faster than the standard cadence, we can pursue an expedited purge for an additional operational fee and a confirmed migration window.

Open items for alignment (need internal confirmation below):
1) Can infra confirm the safe window for hard purge job completion under heavy load (we list 24–72h above; confirm upper bound).
2) Legal/Privacy to confirm exception request template and approval SLA.

Listing infra notes inline:

- Hard purge jobs: upper bound 72 hours under peak load; typical completion < 24 hours. We run purge jobs in windows to avoid I/O storms; for expedited requests we can run on-demand ad-hoc purges (requires a support ticket and 2–4 hour maintenance window) — note this is operational and not instantaneous.
- Snapshots: snapshot metadata tombstone is immediate on delete request; physical object cleanup is part of the scheduled prune (180 days). Expedited snapshot purge (pre-180) requires subprocessor coordination and may leave copies in backup provider immutable backups for legal reasons — we will notify customers of these caveats.
- Audit logs: raw request logs live in time-series storage with TTL; extracting logs for an exception request is supported but we will provide a scoped export rather than long-term retention in raw form.
